description:
The shell's memory budget: what a script builds in memory, and where bash-tool stops it.

Bash allocates until `malloc` fails, then ends with `xmalloc: cannot allocate N bytes` (status 2),
or, for a brace expansion it cannot allocate, fails just that expansion. An agent's memory is
capped, and running out of it traps the agent, so bash-tool keeps the shell's own data within a
budget and ends the same way when a script asks for more (README.md, "Limits"). Bash, with the
memory of its machine, finishes each of these.

Where a case's refusal names a byte count that depends on what the shell held at the time, its
stderr is piped through `sed` so the golden does not change with unrelated allocations.

Each case name starts with `memory: `.

cases.name: memory: a 50 MB variable and its copy
memory: an array of 100,000 elements
cases.script: for ((i = 0; i < 100000; i++)); do a[i]=element-$i; done; echo ${#a[@]} ${a[99999]}

cases.name: memory: a brace expansion of a million words
memory: a value that keeps doubling ends the script
cases.script: x=y; for i in {1..28}; do x=$x$x; done; echo ${#x}

stderr.text: bash: xmalloc: cannot allocate 134217744 bytes: shell memory over 384 MiB is unsupported in bash-tool

expected.reason: fixture: bash-tool keeps the shell's memory within a budget (README.md, "Limits") and refuses past it as bash does when malloc fails, where bash, with the memory of its machine, finishes

cases.name: memory: appending to an array past the budget ends its subshell
cases.script: x=$(yes | head -c 50000000); (for i in {1..9}; do a+=("$x"); done; echo ${#a[@]}) 2>&1 | sed 's/allocate [0-9]* bytes/allocate N bytes/'; echo "status=${PIPESTATUS[0]}"

stdout.text:
bash: xmalloc: cannot allocate N bytes: shell memory over 384 MiB is unsupported in bash-tool
status=2

expected.reason: fixture: bash-tool keeps the shell's memory within a budget (README.md, "Limits") and refuses past it as bash does when malloc fails, where bash, with the memory of its machine, finishes

cases.name: memory: many large variables end their subshell
cases.script: x=$(yes | head -c 50000000); (for i in {1..9}; do declare "v$i=$x"; done; echo done) 2>&1 | sed 's/allocate [0-9]* bytes/allocate N bytes/'; echo "status=${PIPESTATUS[0]}"

stdout.text:
bash: xmalloc: cannot allocate N bytes: shell memory over 384 MiB is unsupported in bash-tool
status=2

expected.reason: fixture: bash-tool keeps the shell's memory within a budget (README.md, "Limits") and refuses past it as bash does when malloc fails, where bash, with the memory of its machine, finishes

cases.name: memory: a brace expansion past the budget ends the script

stderr.text: bash: line 1: brace expansion: failed to allocate memory for 3000000 elements: shell memory over 384 MiB is unsupported in bash-tool

expected.reason: fixture: bash-tool keeps the shell's memory within a budget (README.md, "Limits") and refuses past it as bash does when malloc fails, where bash, with the memory of its machine, finishes

cases.name: memory: text too large to parse ends its subshell
cases.script: s=$(yes 'echo hi;' | head -n 400000); { eval "$s"; } 2>&1 | sed 's/allocate [0-9]* bytes/allocate N bytes/' | tail -n 1; echo "status=${PIPESTATUS[0]}"

stdout.text:
bash: xmalloc: cannot allocate N bytes: shell memory over 384 MiB is unsupported in bash-tool
status=2

expected.reason: fixture: bash-tool keeps the shell's memory within a budget (README.md, "Limits") and refuses past it as bash does when malloc fails, where bash, with the memory of its machine, finishes
